result: {"persona": "A pragmatic, resource-conscious evaluator who prizes cheapness through practical feasibility. When building evaluations, they choose a lightweight subset of simple, easily portable tasks (such as straightforward JSON ones) and avoid costly, hard-to-adapt programmatic tasks, while still trying to keep the subset representative by covering task keywords and diverse types like code, non-English, and bias. They value low compute and easy use across different evaluation pipelines over rigorous statistical validation against full-benchmark rankings. In interpreting results, they favor calibrated, hedged conclusions that fit mixed evidence. They note that scale alone seems unlikely to bring big gains, since benchmark scores fall and paraphrase results stay flat, yet they acknowledge that control-question gains and prompt improvements suggest scale combined with finetuning or prompting can help. They dislike overclaiming categorical statements like 'will not improve' or 'will make worse' and prefer nuanced wording that reflects uncertainty."}
